title: Modified Julian Date Clock
intro: Modified Julian Date (MJD) is a shortened continuous day coordinate, defined as Julian Date minus 2400000.5.
structure: The integer part advances at UTC midnight. The decimal fraction measures part of the same uniform 24-hour model day. Three fractional digits resolve 86.4 ordinary seconds and five resolve 0.864 seconds.
example: At the Unix epoch (1 January 1970, 00:00 UTC), MJD is 40587.000; twelve hours later it is 40587.500. At 12:00 UTC on 1 January 2000 it is 51544.500. The higher-precision setting adds two fractional digits.
history: The modified convention provides a shorter day count and a midnight boundary for scientific and engineering records. Its zero corresponds to 17 November 1858, 00:00 on the corresponding civil-day coordinate.
model: Floor-divide signed Unix microseconds by 86400000000; add 40587 to the day quotient, retain a nonnegative day phase and floor its fractional ticks at 1000 or 100000 per day. Format the entire signed scaled value so negative fractions are represented correctly. Schedule the next tick by ceiling division and upward millisecond rounding.
limits: This implementation is a Unix-derived UTC-like coordinate with uniform days; it does not convert to UT1, TT or TDB or apply leap-second corrections. Local time zone and location do not alter the display.
